title: Clinical observational trial for evaluation of the efficiency of different defect treatments after resection of basal cell carcinoma in face and head area
summary:
Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most frequent skin tumor type in Germany. BCCs are mostly located in body areas exposed to sun light. 
BCC tumors are slowly growing and locally destructive tumors, but with only rare occurrence of metastases. Therefore, the therapeutic focus lies on the tumor area. Gold standard for treatment of so-called white skin cancer is surgery. However, due to necessary safety margins functional and esthetic restrictions as consequence are possible. Therefore, in some cases the surgeon decides against total surgical removal. 
Basal cell carcinoma can be composed of different types of carcinoma cell, which can be microscopically distinguished. Some have a higher probability to lead to new tumors in the original area. In clinical studies it has been shown that recurring BCCs (so-called recurrences) are often much more aggressive than the original tumor. In such a case a further surgery is necessary, this time with a much more extended safety margin. Total removal of the BCC within the primary surgery is therefore highly recommended. The resulting wound is nowadays treated with either skin transplants, biomaterials (certified for intended use), or adjacent skin, which is shifted to cover the wound.
Aim of this study is now to compare the different treatment possibilities for wound closure after tumor resection surgery and to analyzed if there are connections between treatment and therapeutic outcome of tumor therapy. The so gained data shall be used for generation of a data base for improved therapy planning and treatment of upcoming patients. Data collected will be age, gender, data of the tumor and the therapy, and data of previous and concomitant diseases.

interventions.name:
Single-stage defect treatment - primary wound closure post BCC resection surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Single-stage defect treatment - Full thickness /Split skin graft transplantation for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Single-stage defect treatment - Biomaterial (certified for intended use) for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Single-stage defect treatment - Biomaterial (certified for intended use) in combination with skin graft transplantation for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Two-stage defect treatment - primary wound closure for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Two-stage defect treatment - Full thickness /Split skin graft transplantation for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery in a second surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Two-stage defect treatment - Biomaterial (certified for intended use)  for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery in a second surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

Two-stage defect treatment - Biomaterial (certified for intended use) in combination with skin graft transplantation  for wound coverage post BCC resection surgery in a second surgery
[Evaluation of clinical and demographic parameter pre-, intra- and post-surgery up to 12 months post-surgery]

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Informed consent; Primary diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma or pre-treated basal cell carcinoma; Patient is able and willing to follow study related instructions
Exclusion criteria:
patients with immunosuppression; hereditary disorders (genetic dermatosis); inability to follow post-surgery instructions; inability to attend follow-up visits; inability to follow study-related instructions
